name: Stride Inc
business: Provides online K-12 curriculum, virtual school management, career learning and adult skills training, mainly to public school districts and families in the US.

events.what: CEO and Chair James J. Rhyu departed (both roles; he did NOT move to Chairman). Board-initiated: 'the board determined that for Stride to reach its full potential, a new leader was needed'. Stock fell about 15% to 18% on the announcement per analyst on the call.
events.from: Stride independent director (since 2018 per Knowling; resigned 2025-04-15 and rejoined 2025-09-16 per 8-Ks); former CEO of Covad Communications, Telwares, NYC Leadership Academy

events.what: New independent Chair of the Board appointed
New director elected (audit and compensation committees)
events.from: former President and CEO, CSG Systems International

events.what: Knowling re-elected to the board (board expanded from seven to eight), after resigning 2025-04-15

next_event.source: CFO Blackman, Q4 FY2026 call, 2026-08-04 (doc 128966): 'we will provide formal enrollment and financial guidance when we report our first quarter results in October.' First guidance under the new CEO; exact date not found. No Investor Day announced.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: The FY2028 framework (Investor Day 2023-11-14) is a dollar range for adjusted operating income ($415M to $585M) on revenue of $2.7B to $3.3B, not a margin level. Implied AOI margin is 15.4% (low) to 17.7% (high), 16.7% at the midpoint, which is BELOW the 19.8% AOI margin already delivered in FY2026. It frames no margin expansion. The CFO reaffirmed 'on track' on 2026-08-04 under the new CEO. Stride's EBITDA margin (24.5% LTM) is at, not below, the industry median (24.7%).

statements.quote: Based upon those factors, I expect that our revenue for 2028 will be between $2.7 billion and $3.3 billion. We expect AOI to be between $415 million and $585 million, EPS to be between $6.15 and $8.30.
statements.speaker: Donna Blackman

statements.quote: We believe the foundation we've built positions us well for the coming year, and we believe we are on track to achieve our FY 2028 financial targets.
statements.speaker: Donna Blackman

statements.quote: Ultimately, the board determined that for Stride to reach its full potential, a new leader was needed to take the reins.
statements.speaker: Bob Knowling

statements.quote: We expect growth margins will be flattish to last year
statements.speaker: Donna Blackman

street.gap_assumption: June fiscal year end; Baba labels match company fiscal years (FY2028 = year ending June 2028). FY2026 is actual. Compares the target-implied AOI margin at the midpoint ($500M / $3.0B = 16.67%) with FY2028 consensus operating income / revenue ($544.9M / $2,684.1M = 20.30%). Even the high end ($585M / $3.3B = 17.7%) is about 257 bps below consensus. In dollars, consensus FY2028 AOI $544.9M already sits inside the $415M to $585M range; consensus revenue $2.68B is just below the $2.7B floor. Only 3 brokers.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q3 FY2026, Q4 FY2026], AOI margin from VA operating income. FY2026 gross margin 37.8%, down 140 bps on platform implementation costs (Blackman, doc 128966); FY2026 AOI margin 19.8% vs 19.4% FY2025 on lower SG&A. FY2027 guide: gross margin flattish; formal guidance in October. The problem at Stride is enrollment and revenue (Gen Ed down 2.5%, Roscoe ISD contract loss), not margin.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: the FY2028 framework implies a 16.7% AOI margin (midpoint), below both the 19.8% already achieved and the 20.3% FY2028 consensus; consensus AOI $544.9M is inside the $415M to $585M range. Margins are also at the industry median, so the below-peer margin premise does not hold.
verdict: Real GXO-style leadership catalyst (board-forced CEO change two months ago, new Chair, new director) on a stock down 54%, but it is a growth and enrollment story, not a margin gap; the 2028 framework is already exceeded on margin.
open_questions: Does Knowling reset or withdraw the FY2028 framework with the first FY2027 guide in October 2026, and does it include any margin or cost target?
What drove the board to remove Rhyu, and does the platform rollout that cost 140 bps of gross margin in FY2026 have further costs?
How much enrollment is lost with Roscoe ISD and the closed in-year enrollment windows?
